evidence: Cic. Par. 34: quid est enim lībertās? potestās vīvendī ut velīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Freedom as against slavery, and the liberty of a people that governs itself; also freedom to do something, with a genitive (lībertās vīvendī, Cic. Verr. 2.3.3), and frankness of speech (Lewis & Short). Freedom of speech is jūs līberē loquendī (M-O s.v. rights: freedom of speech).

terms.gloss: freedom to do as one likes; licence
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.103: puerīs nōn omnem lūdendī licentiam damus
Ter. Heaut. 483: dēteriōrēs omnēs sumus licentiā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Leave to do as one pleases, from licet; then the liberty one takes, and very often unrestrained liberty, licence, lack of discipline (Lewis & Short). Use it for permission and for too much freedom, not for political freedom, which is lībertās.

phrases.latin: quam dulcis sit lībertās, breviter prōloquar.
phrases.english: how sweet freedom is, I shall tell you in a few words.

phrases.latin: omnēs autem hominēs nātūrā lībertātī studēre et condiciōnem servitūtis ōdisse
phrases.english: but all men by nature long for freedom and hate the condition of slavery

phrases.latin: mox sēgnitia cum ōtiō intrāvit, āmissā virtūte pariter ac lībertāte
phrases.english: then sloth came in with ease, and courage and freedom were lost together

phrases.latin: ut enim puerīs nōn omnem lūdendī licentiam damus, sed eam quae ab honestātis āctiōnibus nōn sit aliēna
phrases.english: for as we don’t give children every freedom to play, but only the kind that is not out of keeping with good conduct
